title: Constructive Simonovits — A Polynomial-Time Algorithm for Forced Saturated Planar Subgraphs

problemStatement.formal: \exists\, \mathcal{A} \text{ running in } \operatorname{poly}(n) \text{ time such that, given } G = (V,E) \text{ with } |V| = n \text{ and } |E| \ge \left\lfloor \tfrac{n^2}{4} \right\rfloor + \left\lfloor \tfrac{n+1}{2} \right\rfloor, \; \mathcal{A}(G) \text{ outputs } H \subseteq G \text{ with } H \cong K_4 \text{ or } H \cong C_\ell + 2K_1\ (\ell \ge 3).
problemStatement.plain: Simonovits proved every n-vertex graph with at least floor(n^2/4) + floor((n+1)/2) edges contains a saturated planar subgraph on more than three vertices: either a K_4 or a cycle C_ell with two extra vertices each joined to the whole cycle (C_ell + 2K_1). His proof shows such a subgraph exists but does not obviously say how to find one efficiently. The question is whether the proof can be made fully constructive, yielding a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that actually outputs one of these two structures on such dense graphs.
whyMatters: Converting extremal existence proofs into polynomial-time algorithms is a central theme in combinatorics (algorithmic regularity lemma, constructive Lovasz Local Lemma); a constructive Simonovits theorem would fit this program and yield certificate-producing witnesses.

Both target subgraphs are saturated planar (|E| = 3|V| - 6), so an efficient finder produces explicit maximal-planar witnesses inside dense graphs and sharpens where forced topological structure lives.

knownResults: Simonovits's dichotomy (existence) is the parent gallery result erdos-1019 (axiom simonovits_theorem).
The K_4 branch is already constructive: fixed-subgraph search runs in O(n^4). The open difficulty is the C_ell + 2K_1 branch where ell is unbounded.
Threshold tightness: Erdos's construction with floor(n^2/4) + floor((n-1)/2) edges avoids all such subgraphs; the one-edge gap is exact.
references: M. Simonovits, A method for solving extremal problems in graph theory, Theory of Graphs (Tihany, 1966), 279-319.
P. Erdos, M. Simonovits, A limit theorem in graph theory, Studia Sci. Math. Hungar. 1 (1966), 51-57.
N. Alon et al., The algorithmic aspects of the regularity lemma, J. Algorithms 16 (1994), 80-109.
